To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we used integrative dynamic structural techniques to reveal the essential dynamics and conformers of a GTPase that are essential for its oligomerization and that we could show that this process is controlled by a GTP induced association of the G domain and by the assembly dependent hydrolysis of GTP.
the essential dynamics of the effector domain of hGBP1 is essential for the GTP controlled reversible oligomerization of hGBP1 and the subsequent formation and dissolution of condensates.
the C-terminal effector domain of hGBP1 is flexible and that the essential conformational changes are triggered by GTP binding.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the structural and functional characterization of the human GTPase GBP1.
the dynamic structural biology of hGBP1 and its oligomerization in solution and the resulting condensates.
the dynamic structural basis and mechanism how hGBP1 as an important member of the innate immune response to viral infections and cancer cells oligomerizes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we identified the structural basis of the GTP controlled oligomeric assembly process of hGBP1 and its functional relevance in the innate immune system by integrative dynamic structural methods.

the dynamic structural biology of hGBP1 reveals a GTP independent intrinsic flexibility of the C terminus and a GTP dependent association of the G domains that control hGBP1's reversible oligomerization and assembly into condensates.

we have shown the essential dynamics of a large GPTase in solution and have identified conformers that are important for its function and that we have used integrative dynamic structural methods to do so.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have discovered the structural basis of the GTP controlled oligomeric assembly of a large G protein and that this is achieved through a GTP induced association and dissociation of the GTP binding domain.
we have shown that the GBP's GTPase domains are flexible and that they are the key to oligomerization.
integrative dynamic structural analysis of large GTPases reveals the essential dynamics of sub domains and conformers essential to the oligomerization mechanism.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we can use integrative structural biology to study large protein complexes and their dynamics in solution.

integrative structural biology can be applied to large systems with a high level of structural complexity and that the combination of neutron scattering with X ray scattering and spectroscopic methods can be a powerful tool to understand the dynamic structure and dynamics of large proteins.
we can now understand how the large GTPase hGBP1 can switch from an inactive state to an oligomerized active state.
